title: VVIP: Versatile Vertical Indexing Processor for Edge Computing
problem: Conventional SIMD processors lack efficient support for sparse data operations and multibit-serial multiplication, requiring significant area overhead for data reordering. Edge computing applications need processors that can handle both regular compute-intensive tasks and irregular sparse workloads without substantial hardware complexity.
motivation: Edge devices require high-performance processors that efficiently support diverse workloads including linear algebra and sparse operations while maintaining minimal area overhead.
method: VVIP implements a SIMD architecture with customized vertical source and destination indexing instructions that enable efficient data reordering within processing modules using data-steering logic and registers. Register files are leveraged as lookup tables or accumulators to support multibit-serial multiplication and sparse data operations. The design was verified on a vector processor implementation.
key_novelty: Vertical indexing instructions that enable efficient data reordering and sparse operation support within SIMD processors using minimal area overhead.
contributions: Vertical source and destination indexing instructions for area-efficient SIMD data reordering
Support for multibit-serial multiplication leveraging register files as lookup tables
Efficient sparse data operation support using data-steering logic
Achieved 10.1x speedup on linear algebra and 1.2x on sparse convolution with <2.8% area overhead

metrics.speedup: 10.1x vs 1-bit-serial multiplication on linear algebra; 1.2x on sparse point-wise convolution

primary_theme: SIMD processor with specialized indexing for efficient edge computing
